### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.deps

### Question

I have an update script that updates various packages, etc. on MacOS. I would like to also update Neovim plugins.

To do this I currently run:

```bash
nvim --headless -c +'lua MiniDeps.update(nil, { force = true })' +TSUpdateSync +qa
```

However this doesn't seem to do the trick. It downloads the updates but doesn't seem to install them. When I run this and run `:DepsUpdate` from Neovim afterwards I get the usual buffer where I need to `:w` to install the updates.

Is it possible doing headless updates?

comment_data.body:
Running this exact command seems to have worked for me:

```bash
nvim --headless -c +'lua MiniDeps.update(nil, { force = true })' +TSUpdateSync +qa
```

The trick here is that it *only* updates plugins which are currently added to the session (with default `nil`). I.e. the ones which you [add with `now`](https://github.com/KimNorgaard/dotfiles/blob/c89c4369ef402c729e6789a54c6f54967998fc7f/.config/nvim/lua/plugins.lua#L25). The ones [added with `later`](https://github.com/KimNorgaard/dotfiles/blob/c89c4369ef402c729e6789a54c6f54967998fc7f/.config/nvim/lua/plugins.lua#L135) are not yet in session during this way of `MiniDeps.update()` execution.

Running that command did take some time (as usual as with interactive "in-session" update) and indeed updated plugins that were loaded with `now()`.

> However this doesn't seem to do the trick. It downloads the updates but doesn't seem to install them.

Let's check this more thoroughly:
- What does `:DepsShowLog` show after executing the CLI command with `update`? It should contain an entry like `========== Update 2025-03-13 20:12:13 ==========` with plugins that are added with `now` (even if they didn't have any updates).
- What is the state (Git commit) of actually updated plugins? For example, I had an log entry that showed updates to `nvim-treesitter`. I navigated to '~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/deps/opt/nvim-treesitter' and it indeed showed that its on the latest commit from the update (i.e. updates did apply as expected).

reply_data.body: I wonder if wrapping `MiniDeps.update()` in `vim.schedule` would force it to run later?
reply_data.bodyHTML: I wonder if wrapping MiniDeps.update() in vim.schedule would force it to run later?
reply_data.bodyText: I wonder if wrapping MiniDeps.update() in vim.schedule would force it to run later?

reply_data.body:
> I wonder if wrapping `MiniDeps.update()` in `vim.schedule` would force it to run later?

If anything, it should be `MiniDeps.later()` instead of `vim.schedule()`.

> So the question is if there is a way forward/around here or if it's by design/too much work? It's probably not the most wide spread use case :)

Only hacky workaround, I am afraid. After trial and error, something like this should work:

```bash
nvim --headless -c +"lua MiniDeps.later(function() MiniDeps.update(nil, { force = true }); vim.cmd('TSUpdateSync'); vim.cmd('qa') end); vim.wait(30000)"
```

What it does:
- Registers a `later()` callback (which should be executed after all `later()` callbacks from the 'init.lua') and asks Neovim to wait for 30 seconds until proceeding.
- The `later()` callback does force update which is done non-blocking but synchronously (i.e. it is not going to the next line/command until this one is finished; I now vaguely remember that this particular headless case was the motivation behind this design). Only *after* that `:TSUpdateSync` is run followed by `qa!`.

---

Note for clarity and possibly future self. Using "all plugins in session" as default for `MiniDeps.update()` is mostly motivated by the fact that using "all plugins in '~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/deps/'" has the following caveats:
- A use case of "I want to have many plugins available but load only handful" seems like a valid one. So if the user previously run `:DepsAdd author/plugin` for a quick look at a plugin, it would still be updated during `update()` even if not currently loaded.
- Plugins not in session do not define `checkout` target. It is possible to use default target for them (i.e. usually `master` or `main`), but it might conflict with previous uses of the plugin.

An opposite problem here with using "all plugins in session" is this question: if plugin is added with `later()`, it can not be easily updated with "headless approach". But as there *is* a workaround, it might be not that bad. I can not think of other downsides of this approach.

None of these points are huge problems, but mostly contribute to a design decision.
